questions.question: In the survey of 50 learners (24 netball, 18 tennis, 10 both), which region of the Venn diagram must be filled FIRST?
options: The overlap, with 10 — because the totals 24 and 18 both already include those learners

questions.question: With the overlap holding 10, the netball-only and tennis-only regions hold:
How many of the 50 learners play neither sport?
The audit that certifies a completed two-event Venn diagram is:
options: the two circles are the same size
the overlap is the smallest number
each circle totals more than the overlap
all four regions together total the sample space: 14 + 10 + 8 + 18 = 50

questions.question: The addition rule states that P(A or B) equals:
For the survey, P(netball or tennis) is:
The subtraction in the addition rule exists because:
options: probabilities must always be made smaller
adding whole circles counts the overlap twice, so it must be removed once
OR means only one of the events may happen

questions.question: Given P(A) = 0,5, P(B) = 0,35 and P(A or B) = 0,7, then P(A and B) is:
Two events are mutually exclusive when:
options: they share no outcomes — they can never happen together
together they cover the whole sample space

questions.question: On a Venn diagram, mutually exclusive events appear as:
options: two circles with a large overlap
two separated circles — the intersection region does not exist

questions.question: A card is drawn from a box of cards numbered 1 to 10. P(below 3 or above 8) is:
options: 2/10 + 2/10 = 4/10 = 2/5, since the events are mutually exclusive
1, because every card is either below 3 or above 8

questions.question: Why must you justify mutual exclusivity before using P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B)?
options: Because the short rule always gives smaller answers
Because the short rule is only for spinners and cards
Because on overlapping events the short rule double-counts the overlap and can even push an answer past 1

subtopics.title: Complementary Events and Full Machinery Problems

questions.question: Complementary events are events that are:
options: mutually exclusive AND exhaustive — no overlap, and together they cover the whole sample space
any two events whose probabilities add to less than 1

questions.question: The card events 'below 3' and 'above 8' are mutually exclusive but NOT complementary because:
options: the cards 3 to 8 belong to neither event, so the pair fails to cover the sample space

questions.question: For the survey, P(neither sport) computed two ways gives:
options: 18/50 = 0,36 directly, and 1 − 0,64 = 0,36 by the complement — both agree

questions.question: P(exactly one of the two sports) uses which regions?
options: Netball-only plus tennis-only: (14 + 8)/50 = 22/50 — the overlap is excluded

subtopics.title: Two Ropes in the School Hall

questions.question: In the hall, a learner who plays both netball and tennis stands:
options: with one foot in each ring
in the lens where the two ropes cross — inside both rings at once

questions.question: Why do the ten both-players walk to the lens FIRST when staging the survey?
options: Because they are hiding inside both team totals — placing them first lets each remaining count be found by subtraction
Because the lens is in the middle of the hall
Because the lens is the largest region

questions.question: A learner standing inside the taped rectangle but outside both ropes represents:
options: a learner who plays both sports
a learner outside the sample space
a learner in the grade who plays neither sport

questions.question: The registers say 24 netball and 18 tennis, yet only 32 learners stand inside rope. The 10 phantoms exist because:
options: the lens learners appear on BOTH registers — adding registers counts memberships, not people
the registers were out of date
netball players were counted at double weight

questions.question: The one-move repair for the double-count is:
options: remove the lens learners from both registers

questions.question: If skipping the subtraction pushes a 'probability' beyond 1, that signals:
options: the sample space was too small
the answer should be rounded down to 1
an overlap was double-counted — the addition rule's built-in alarm has gone off

questions.question: Rope rings pulled completely apart, sharing no floor, picture events that are:
options: mutually exclusive — 'both' is not a place that exists

questions.question: The open-floor test says complementary events require:
options: some learners left standing on open floor
no overlap AND no open floor — everyone stands in exactly one of the two regions
at least one learner in the lens

questions.question: 'Below 3' and 'above 8' on the 1-to-10 card box are exclusive but not complementary because:
options: no card can be both, but complementary pairs must involve exactly two cards
the cards 3 to 8 are left standing on the open floor — the pair leaves leftovers
